 Up Helly Aa 2027 in Lerwick: the Shetland fire festival 
 Culture Up Helly Aa 2027 in Lerwick: the Shetland fire festival 
 Up Helly Aa 2027 in Lerwick on Tuesday 26 January: official programme, tickets, NorthLink ferry, UK ETA and alcohol rules, dated and sourced.
 Updated November 16, 2026 
 15 min read 
 Contents
 Loading… 
 Commercial partnership . This article contains affiliate links. If you book through these links, Pixidia earns a small commission at no extra cost to you.
 Learn more Partners: Viator Up Helly Aa 2027 takes place on Tuesday 26 January 2027 in Lerwick, Shetland. The torchlit procession leaves Hillhead at 7:30 pm. It is free and open to everyone; only the halls charge admission, and the Town Hall ticket cost £50 at the 2026 price.
 Checked on 16 November 2026 against the official sources cited (Up Helly Aa committee, Visit Shetland, NorthLink, gov.uk). 
 Every last Tuesday of January, Lerwick, the capital of Shetland, burns a replica longship at the end of a torchlit procession. In 2027, the festival falls on Tuesday 26 January. This guide follows the programme published by the organising committee, the tickets, the access from Aberdeen or Sumburgh, the weather and the rules that matter to a visitor. Key figures carry their source and the date we checked them, and points not yet published for 2027 are flagged as such.
 1. The official 2027 programme, hour by hour
Photo by Simon Hurry 
on Unsplash Lerwick, a day set by the committee
 Free procession 
 Tuesday 26 January 2027 
 Late January, cold and windy 
 Evening from 7:30 pm The 2027 programme runs from the Jarl Squad’s departure at 8:15 am to the first hall visit at 9:15 pm. In the morning, the guizers march in costume, pull the galley and read the Bill, the satirical proclamation that sums up the year. In the afternoon, the Jarl Squad visits the museum, and the squads visit schools, hospitals and care homes; the committee gives no fixed time for these visits or for lunch. In the evening, the torchlit procession sets off from Hillhead.
 Highlights
 The Bill is posted at the Market Cross from 6:00 am to 5:00 pm: it is the satirical text of the year, worth reading before the day. 
 The procession needs no ticket: only the halls charge admission. 
 Visit Shetland advises being in place before 7:00 pm to find a spot along the route. 
 Pixidia tip: plan your morning. The march and the Bill are free and set the tone for the day, while hall times have not been published. To see Lerwick before nightfall, a private car tour lasts 6 hours 30 minutes. Viator offers it on 26 January 2027 with departures at 8:30 am, 9:00 am, 9:30 am and 10:00 am, based on availability checked on 16 November 2026. Viator states a full refund if you cancel at least 24 hours before departure; the listing also mentions a 30-day rule, so check the rule shown when you book.
 Full-Day Private City Tour in Lerwick ★ 4.9 · 42  reviews Partner link 
 On 26 January 2027: €419.09 per person (based on 2 adults), checked on 16 November 2026 €419.09 per person On 26 January 2027: (based on 2 adults), checked on 16 November 2026 
 See dates Official Up Helly Aa 2027 programme, Tuesday 26 January 2027, in Lerwick Time What happens Where 
 6:00 am The Bill is posted (until 5:00 pm) Market Cross 
 8:15 am Jarl Squad departs Islesburgh Community Centre 
 9:40 am British Legion departs, pause in front of the Bill Esplanade, Commercial Street, Market Cross 
 10:30 am Departure for the civic reception (by invitation) Bressay Ferry Terminal 
 3:30 pm Jarl Squad visits the museum Shetland Museum

 9:15 pm First hall visit of the evening (halls not named) Halls 
 Source: official Up Helly Aa 2027 programme , checked on 16 November 2026. The junior procession leaves Hillhead at 5:30 pm according to the committee’s day page : that is a 2026 reference, and no 2027 time has been published. 
 2. Tickets and halls: what you buy, and what you don’t
 The procession is open to the public and needs no ticket. Tickets are for the halls, where each squad performs its sketch and sings through the night. Around a dozen halls host the squads, and most of them are private.
 The only hall whose tickets the committee sells is the Lerwick Town Hall: £50 per ticket, first come, first served, according to the committee’s tickets page checked on 16 November 2026. That is the 2026 price: the 2027 price has not been published.
 Demand for 2026 is closed. The committee invites people to come back later in 2026 for the 2027 edition, with no opening date announced. For the other halls, ticketing depends on each host, and no price is published. Visit Shetland describes these places as « extremely limited » and notes that returned tickets can appear in the days before the festival.
 Pixidia tip: if the Town Hall matters to you, watch the committee’s tickets page from late 2026. Otherwise, the procession and the streets of Lerwick remain open without a ticket. 3. Getting there: NorthLink ferry or a flight to Sumburgh
 Two routes link Lerwick to the rest of the UK. The most direct from the mainland is the NorthLink ferry from Aberdeen, which sails overnight. The flight lands at Sumburgh, about 40 km from Lerwick, so you need a further land transfer. If you pass through Edinburgh before heading to Aberdeen, our guide to the best Edinburgh tours helps fill the day.
 For winter 2027, NorthLink’s published timetable shows a departure from Aberdeen at 7:00 pm on most days. The ship goes into dry dock from 10 to 23 January 2027, and the timetable changes during that period.
 NorthLink ferry between Aberdeen and Lerwick, winter 2027 Direction Departs Arrives Dates Note 
 Aberdeen to Lerwick 7:00 pm (5:00 pm via Kirkwall) 7:30 am 2 to 31 January 2027 Outside the dry dock period (10 to 23 January) 
 Lerwick to Aberdeen 7:00 pm or 5:30 pm 7:00 am Same period To be reconfirmed 
 Dry dock Timetable changed Timetable changed 10 to 23 January 2027 Check before booking 
 Source: NorthLink timetable 2027 , checked on 16 November 2026. 
 To arrive on the morning of Tuesday 26 January, you need to board at Aberdeen on the evening of Monday 25. The return sailing from Lerwick still needs reconfirming: the published timetable shows 7:00 pm or 5:30 pm.
 Fares vary by category and period. A press announcement dated 8 September 2026 mentions an increase for 2027 without naming the category, so no amount is published here. Check NorthLink’s official fare list before you book.
 On the flight side, one aggregator lists bus route 6 between Viking bus station and Sumburgh Airport, via Cunningsburgh and Sandwick. These times are old and unverified: check with ZetTrans before relying on them. Loganair opens bookings for summer 2027, but no winter timetable has been found.
 For accommodation, sources talk of booking « several months ahead », sometimes a year for the most sought-after places (Visit Shetland, NorthLink). No availability figure is published.
 4. The torchlit procession and the lighting of the galley
 Illustration: torchlit procession (Pixidia media library photo, not taken in Lerwick) From Hillhead to the burning ground
 7:30 pm 
 Torches lit together 
 About 30 minutes 
 Burning site closed The Jarl Squad walks through the guizers’ ranks at 7:15 pm. The senior procession sets off at 7:30 pm from Hillhead, beneath the Town Hall, and follows the official route. According to Visit Shetland , the march lasts about 30 minutes: a short time, played out in the crowd. The committee’s day page, which gives no year, says more than 900 senior torches are lit together at a signal of smoke.
 The galley, the replica longship built by the committee, is parked at Bressay Ferry Terminal until 6:00 pm, then joins Hillhead for the procession. It is burned at the end of the march, on the King George V playing field.
 According to the same committee page, the burning site is closed to the public and the press. 
 The junior procession leaves Hillhead at 5:30 pm: that is the 2026 reference, and no 2027 time has been published. 
 Pixidia tip: the committee warns that the heat is intense at the front. Keep your distance from the flames. 5. Weather and clothing: preparing for a January night
Photo by ella peebles 
on Unsplash Late January: cold, wind and damp
 Cold 
 Wind 
 Damp 
 Snow possible In late January, Lerwick is cold, windy and often damp, with snow at times. No temperature figure is given here, because the averages we found differ depending on the source. The committee points out there is no postponement in bad weather: the festival goes ahead whatever the forecast. If the night sky also draws you, our guide to the northern lights in Scotland for winter 2026-2027 covers viewing conditions in mainland Scotland.
 What to pack
 Warm layers and a waterproof, windproof jacket, to get through the waiting times. 
 Comfortable shoes: the procession and the halls are on foot, and the evening is long. 
 A well-charged phone for photos and navigation, as several visitors’ accounts report. 
 Pixidia tip: the day is long, from the morning until the early hours of Wednesday. Plan a meal in mid-afternoon and a rest, as Visit Shetland advises. 6. Formalities and rules: ETA, alcohol and the next day
 The UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
 You apply for the ETA online on gov.uk . It costs £20, the amount shown on the official page checked on 16 November 2026. The rise from £16 to £20 was announced for April 2026 by the press (The Local).
 The gov.uk page says that visitors from Europe and the USA usually need an ETA rather than a visa, and that every traveller needs their own, children included. British and Irish passport holders do not need one. Whether you need one depends on your nationality, so check the eligibility checker on gov.uk before you book, including if you enter the UK through Aberdeen.
 Pixidia tip: don’t rely on an old fee. Only the gov.uk page counts. Drinking in the street: don’t count on it
 Lerwick’s byelaw has banned drinking in unlicensed public places since 2007. The press mentions an exception during Up Helly Aa, but no published wording specifies it. A review launched in 2023 has not, to date, produced a published decision. So assume that drinking in the street is not allowed, and check the current rules with Shetland Islands Council before you travel.
 The next day, Wednesday 27 January 2027
 Wednesday 27 January is a public holiday for Shetland Islands Council employees and, according to the press, for part of Lerwick. Some shops in town stay closed, while those outside Lerwick generally open. An old blog says Lerwick’s two supermarkets stay open, but this still needs confirming. So do your shopping before Tuesday evening.
 7. Origins and debates: a recent festival in ancient dress
 Up Helly Aa’s Viking look is younger than it seems. Before 1870, Shetland marked Yule at New Year and Candlemas, and kept the Julian calendar until the late 19th century. Tar barrels, judged dangerous, were abandoned between about 1874 and 1880. The first torchlit Yule procession dates from 1876, and the first galley joined the procession in 1889.
 In 1894, Haldane Burgess published The Viking Path , which set the festival’s Viking theme. Historians remain cautious: the Norse dimension is a late 19th-century construction, grafted onto older fire festivals. Some blogs trace the roots back to 1815, but academic work and museum publications are more sceptical.
 The liveliest debate concerns women’s place in the festival. The committee lifted the gender restriction for future editions in 2022; women became guizers in squads in 2023, and the Jarl Squad opened to women in 2024, according to press coverage at the time. Dates vary from one article to another, so go by the committee’s timeline of decisions rather than a single article.
 Squads are reserved for residents: to take part in one, you must have lived in Shetland for five years, according to an extract from the committee’s page. Visitors attend the festival; they do not take part as guizers.
 8. Indicative budget
 The budget comes down to a few known costs. The procession is free. The only verified amounts are the ETA, £20 on gov.uk if it applies to you, and the Town Hall ticket, £50 at the 2026 price (the 2027 price is not published). The rest (ferry, flight, accommodation, other halls) is not priced for 2027.
 Verified or announced costs for Up Helly Aa 2027, checked on 16 November 2026 Item Amount Status 
 Procession Free Verified, committee’s day page 
 Town Hall ticket £50 2026 price, 2027 not published 
 Other halls Not published Gap 
 UK ETA (if it applies) £20 Verified, gov.uk 
 Aberdeen-Lerwick ferry Not priced here 2027 fare schedule not read 
 Accommodation Not priced Gap 
 Sources: Up Helly Aa committee tickets , committee day page , gov.uk , checked on 16 November 2026. 
 To keep costs down, count only the amounts above, and treat the free procession as the centrepiece of the evening. As for cash, no source confirms whether cash machines or card terminals will work on the day, so carrying some cash remains general advice.
 9. Depending on your profile
 First time. Focus the evening on the procession: arrive before 7:00 pm, stand along the route, and keep the next day free, since part of Lerwick’s shopping stays closed.
 Heritage lovers. The Shetland Museum welcomes the Jarl Squad at 3:30 pm, and the Bill goes up at the Market Cross from 6:00 am. The morning is when the tradition is easiest to read, before the night of the halls.
 Families. The junior festival takes place the same day, with a children’s procession that leaves Hillhead at 5:30 pm according to the 2026 reference. The 2027 time has not been published: check the committee’s page before you travel.
 Tight budget. The procession needs no ticket. The main cost is the ferry or the flight. The 2027 fare is not in an official schedule we could read, and the dry dock from 10 to 23 January changes the ferry timetable: compare sailing times early.
 Reduced mobility. No accessibility information specific to the procession or the halls appears in the sources we checked (see the FAQ). Write to the committee before you come.
 10. The other fire festivals in the islands in 2027
 Around a dozen rural fire festivals take place between January and March across the islands, with the same ritual and fewer visitors. Scalloway opens the season on 8 January 2027. For another Scottish evening in January, our Burns Night 2027 guide covers the supper and its dates.
 Fire festivals in Shetland in 2027, according to Visit Shetland and the committee Date Festival Status

 5 February 2027 Nesting and Girlsta Listed by Visit Shetland

 Source: Visit Shetland, fire festivals , checked on 16 November 2026; Lerwick date, Up Helly Aa committee . 
 What other guides don’t tell you yet for 2027
 The 2027 price of the Town Hall ticket is not published: only the 2026 price, £50, appears on the committee’s tickets page , checked on 16 November 2026. 
 The junior procession leaves Hillhead at 5:30 pm according to the committee’s day page , but that time is a 2026 reference: no 2027 time is published, checked on 16 November 2026. 
 The NorthLink ferry goes into dry dock from 10 to 23 January 2027, according to the NorthLink 2027 timetable , checked on 16 November 2026. 
 The gov.uk ETA page describes eligibility in general terms (Europe, the USA and others), so check your own nationality before you book, checked on 16 November 2026. 
 Practical information in brief
 Formalities UK ETA at £20: check on gov.uk whether it applies to you.
 Getting there NorthLink ferry from Aberdeen or flight to Sumburgh (see section 3). Dry dock from 10 to 23 January.
 The next day Wednesday 27 January: part of the shops stay closed (see section 6).
 Frequently asked questions about Up Helly Aa 2027
 When is Up Helly Aa in 2027? Tuesday 26 January 2027, according to the committee’s official page . The festival falls on the last Tuesday of January every year. Wednesday 27 January is a public holiday for Shetland Islands Council employees and, according to the press, for part of Lerwick.
 How much does a ticket for Up Helly Aa cost? The procession is free and open to the public. Only the halls charge admission. The Town Hall, sold directly by the committee, cost £50 at the 2026 price. The other halls set their own prices, and none has been published for 2027.
 How do I get a ticket for the Town Hall? The committee sells tickets first come, first served. Demand for 2026 is closed, and the committee invites people to come back later in 2026 for the 2027 edition, with no opening date announced. Keep an eye on the tickets page : Visit Shetland also reports returned tickets in the days before the festival.
 What time does the procession start? The senior procession leaves Hillhead at 7:30 pm, with the lighting of the torches. The Jarl Squad walks through the ranks at 7:15 pm. The junior procession leaves at 5:30 pm, a 2026 reference, since no 2027 time is published. Visit Shetland advises arriving before 7:00 pm to find a place.
 How do I get to Lerwick from the mainland? By NorthLink ferry from Aberdeen, departing at 7:00 pm on most days and arriving at 7:30 am from 2 to 31 January 2027, outside the dry dock period. The ship is in dry dock from 10 to 23 January and the timetable changes. By air, Sumburgh is about 40 km from Lerwick; the bus link needs checking with ZetTrans.
 Do I need an ETA to visit? The UK ETA costs £20 and is applied for online on gov.uk . The gov.uk page says visitors from Europe and the USA usually need one, while British and Irish passport holders do not. Check your own nationality on gov.uk before you book.
 Can you drink alcohol in the street during the festival? No, don’t count on it. Lerwick’s byelaw has banned drinking in unlicensed public places since 2007. The press mentions an exception for the festival, but no published wording specifies it, and the review launched in 2023 has not, to date, produced a published decision.
 Are the shops open the day after the festival? Wednesday 27 January 2027 is a public holiday for council employees and, according to the press, for part of Lerwick. Some shops in town stay closed, while those outside Lerwick generally open. An old blog says the two supermarkets stay open: this point still needs confirming.
 What is the weather like, and what should I wear? Late January in Lerwick is cold, windy and often damp, with snow at times (see section 5). The committee points out there is no postponement in bad weather. Pack warm layers, a waterproof, windproof jacket and comfortable shoes for a long evening.
 Is the festival accessible to people with reduced mobility? No accessibility information specific to the procession or the halls appears in the sources we checked. A third-party blog reports disabled parking at several places in Shetland, and partial, or in some places no, wheelchair access. Write to the committee before you come.

 Sources consulted on 16 November 2026. Information from the press is flagged as such in the text.
